# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary | 28 July 2026

The liquidity hierarchy divides sharply into three tiers. The North American leaders—Nasdaq 100 and NYSE—dominate across all metrics, with Nasdaq posting the tightest ILLIQ of 0.0025% per $1M traded and $350.9M comparable volume, while NYSE's 0.6110% AR spread represents the market standard for execution cost. The European mid-pack—Euronext, Xetra, and SIX Swiss—cluster tightly on spreads (0.5427% to 0.5637%) but show modest volumes of $4.0M to $13.9M and higher ILLIQ readings of 0.0310% to 0.0550% per $1M traded. Asia-Pacific presents mixed signals: Tokyo Stock Exchange commands the highest turnover ratio at 2.9248% despite middling ILLIQ of 0.0351% per $1M, while Hong Kong and Korea exchanges lag substantially. The outlier is Korea Exchange, which shows a concerning 1.6313% AR spread—nearly double most peers—alongside elevated ILLIQ of 0.1443% per $1M traded, highlighting structural fragmentation. London Stock Exchange rounds out the bottom tier with the poorest ILLIQ of 0.0827% per $1M traded and weak comparative volume of $9.3M.
